# snapmcp

> Visual documentation MCP server for AI agents and developers. snapmcp renders terminal output, source code, HTTP(S) pages, Markdown, HTML, and diffs into PNG/JPEG, PDF, GIF, Markdown, HTML, PowerPoint, and Word artifacts. It exposes exactly 13 MCP tools. The 12 capture/document tools return saved file paths instead of image bytes; `snapmcp-hint` returns text guidance.

## Use snapmcp when

- a README, tutorial, PR, guide, report, or QA record needs a human-readable visual artifact;
- terminal output or source code should be shown as a polished image;
- a public HTTP(S) page needs a screenshot or print-style PDF;
- several captures must be combined as a batch, ordered sequence, GIF, or captioned document;
- an agent needs a compact way to choose among capture tools.

## Do not use snapmcp when

- the task is browser interaction such as clicking, filling forms, or accessibility-tree navigation; use a browser-automation MCP server;
- the result should be raw structured data rather than a visual artifact;
- the target is an untrusted site and the deployment has no network isolation; the built-in URL checks do not provide complete DNS-rebinding protection.

## Tools

- `capture_terminal`: terminal or CLI output, with `$ ` user prompts and `# ` root prompts; PNG/JPEG.
- `capture_code`: Shiki-highlighted source code for 300+ bundled languages and 27 themes, with optional inclusive `startLine` and `endLine`; PNG/JPEG.
- `capture_browser`: full-page or viewport screenshot of an HTTP(S) URL; PNG/JPEG.
- `capture_file`: syntax-highlighted image of an allowlisted file with optional line range; PNG/JPEG.
- `capture_markdown`: GitHub-flavored Markdown rendered as a document; PNG/JPEG.
- `capture_html`: sanitized HTML/CSS rendered as a document; PNG/JPEG.
- `capture_diff`: unified diff with additions and deletions highlighted; PNG/JPEG.
- `capture_pdf`: complete HTTP(S) URL document rendered with Chromium print/PDF output; PDF.
- `capture_batch`: up to 10 independent captures; image paths.
- `capture_sequence`: up to 60 ordered step images plus an optional GIF; image/GIF paths.
- `capture_gif`: animation from 2 to 60 captures; GIF.
- `capture_document`: up to 30 captioned captures embedded in Markdown, HTML, print-quality PDF, editable PowerPoint, or editable Word; document path.
- `snapmcp-hint`: natural-language tool search and concise agent, setup, security, and token guidance; text.

There is no fourteenth capture tool. Composite tools accept flat discriminated unions: each entry has `type` and the fields for that type at the same level.

## Quick selection

- Terminal or CLI output: `capture_terminal`.
- Source text already in context: `capture_code`.
- File on disk: `capture_file` after `SNAPMCP_ALLOWED_PATHS` is configured.
- Website or web app: `capture_browser`.
- Markdown, HTML, or diff: `capture_markdown`, `capture_html`, or `capture_diff`.
- URL as PDF: `capture_pdf`.
- Independent images: `capture_batch`.
- Ordered tutorial or walkthrough: `capture_sequence`.
- Explicit animation: `capture_gif`.
- Captioned report or guide: `capture_document`.
- Unsure which tool to use: `snapmcp-hint` with a natural-language `query`.

## Discovery

- Canonical MCP catalog: `tools/list`.
- Natural-language MCP search: `snapmcp-hint` with `query`.
- Machine-readable MCP resource: `snapmcp://capabilities`.
- CLI manifest: `snapmcp capabilities --json`.
- CLI intent search: `snapmcp search "<intent>" --json`.
- Static agent guidance: this file and the server instructions.

## Safety and result limits

- URL tools accept HTTP(S) only.
- SSRF protection is default-on: private/local IPv4 and IPv6 literals, IPv4-mapped IPv6, localhost variants, and DNS-resolved private addresses are blocked; requests are revalidated.
- Chromium does not pin the DNS-resolved address, so complete DNS-rebinding prevention is not guaranteed. Isolate hostile targets with network controls.
- File reads are deny-all until `SNAPMCP_ALLOWED_PATHS` is configured.
- Every output stays inside `SNAPMCP_DIR`; traversal and symlink escapes are rejected.
- Synthetic captures render in an isolated browser context with JavaScript disabled, external network resources blocked, and a restrictive CSP. Markdown raw HTML is escaped and raw HTML input is DOM-sanitized. Sanitization is defense in depth, not a perfect-safety guarantee.
- Limits: terminal 1,000 lines; code/Markdown/HTML 200 KB each; diff 500 KB; file 5 MB by default; batch 10; sequence 60; GIF 2 to 60 frames; document 30 captures with up to 25 MB per embedded image and 75 MB total.
- Capture/document results are saved file paths, not image bytes; `snapmcp-hint` returns text guidance.
- Browser profile use is experimental and never selected automatically: URL captures run in the explicitly selected persistent profile context, so profile cookies and session state can be sent to the target site; synthetic captures remain isolated.

## Install and run

Primary runtime: Node.js 20 or newer. Bun 1.2 or newer is optional. npm and npx work without Bun.

```bash
npm install -g snapmcp
snapmcp init
```

`snapmcp init` explicitly installs Playwright Chromium. Package postinstall does not download Chromium. The reproducible browser default is bundled Playwright Chromium; select a system browser explicitly with `SNAPMCP_CHROME_EXECUTABLE`.
